obligation: Bank recall of a misdirected wire (funds response)
citation: Fla. Stat. 670.211 (UCC Article 4A cancellation; Florida worked example); FBI IC3 BEC guidance
trigger: A wire was sent on fraudulent instructions (buyer wire, trust account disbursement, or payoff)
deadline: Immediately on discovery. After the receiving bank accepts the payment order, cancellation works only if that bank agrees, so the first hour matters
notify: Trust account disbursement: the trust bank's wire room (recall request and hold harmless or indemnity letter). Buyer wire: the buyer calls their own bank; the company calls its bank to flag the receiving account
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - operational; not a notification duty
owner: President, Title and Escrow (funds response desk)

obligation: FBI Internet Crime Complaint Center (IC3) complaint
trigger: Any BEC attempt or loss; file regardless of amount
deadline: As soon as possible (voluntary; no legal deadline); same day for any loss
notify: IC3 with full banking details; victims file their own complaints; FBI field office for campaigns

trigger: Acquisition of unencrypted customer information of Title and Escrow without authorization (unauthorized access is presumed to be acquisition unless reliable evidence shows otherwise)
deadline: As soon as possible and no later than 30 days after discovery
notify: FTC through the online form at ftc.gov
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if the event involves 500 or more consumers; count per event, and treat a campaign as one event where counsel concludes it is one
clock_starts: Discovery: first day the event is known to any employee, officer, or other agent other than the person committing it (314.4(j)(2)); contractor agents count
owner: Chief Privacy Officer with the CISO (Qualified Individual)

trigger: FTC notice is required
deadline: With the notice
notify: FTC: name and contact; types of information; date or date range; number of consumers; general description; whether law enforcement gave a written determination that public notice would impede an investigation or harm national security, with contact details

trigger: A law enforcement official determines in writing that public disclosure would impede a criminal investigation or damage national security
deadline: The FTC notice is still filed on time; the official may ask the FTC to delay public disclosure (initial delay up to 30 days, extension up to 60 more days on written request)
notify: State the determination and the official's contact in the FTC notice
clock_starts: Date the FTC notice is provided

citation: Form 8-K Item 1.05; SEC Release 33-11216; 17 CFR 229.106(a) (an incident includes a series of related unauthorized occurrences)
trigger: A cybersecurity incident, or a series of related occurrences, that could be material
deadline: Without unreasonable delay after discovery (the committee convenes within 48 hours of a severity-1 declaration and at least every 2 business days until a decision)
notify: Disclosure committee (General Counsel chairs); record the date, time, and reasoning

trigger: The company determines that a cybersecurity incident is material
deadline: Within 4 business days after the materiality determination
notify: SEC (public filing): material aspects of the nature, scope, and timing, and the material impact or reasonably likely material impact, including on financial condition and results of operations

obligation: SEC filing delay on Attorney General determination
trigger: The U.S. Attorney General determines that disclosure poses a substantial risk to national security or public safety and notifies the SEC in writing
deadline: For the period the Attorney General specifies under Item 1.05(c)
notify: Department of Justice (through outside counsel); the Attorney General notifies the SEC
applies_at_this_tier: Only if the Attorney General so determines

trigger: Annual report on Form 10-K
deadline: With the next Form 10-K; describe whether risks, including from previous incidents, have materially affected or are reasonably likely to materially affect the company
notify: SEC (Form 10-K)

trigger: Disclosure committee convenes on a possibly material incident
deadline: Same day the committee convenes
notify: Committee members, responders with knowledge, and executives
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - company policy, not a regulatory deadline

obligation: State breach notice to individuals (each state of residence)
citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam)
trigger: Breach of personal information of residents, as each state defines it (a mailbox takeover usually exposes account credentials and, for closers, identity and bank data)
deadline: Varies by state: some say without unreasonable delay; some set a fixed number of days
notify: Affected residents of each state
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - apply the law of each state where affected individuals reside; customers live in all 50 states
clock_starts: Varies by state (often determination of a breach)
owner: Chief Privacy Officer with outside counsel

obligation: State attorney general or regulator notice
trigger: Breach above a state-set count of residents, or any breach in some states
deadline: Varies by state
notify: State attorney general or other designated regulator

trigger: Notices above a state-set count
deadline: Varies by state
notify: Nationwide consumer reporting agencies
applies_at_this_tier: Yes where the state threshold is met

obligation: State third-party agent (vendor) notice to the company (inbound)
citation: State breach notification statutes; contract terms under 16 CFR 314.4(f)(2)
trigger: A vendor that maintains personal information for the company has a breach
deadline: Varies by state; standard contract term 10 days
notify: The company (Director of Third-Party Risk Management)

trigger: Breach of security of personal information of Florida residents
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 30 days after the determination of a breach or reason to believe one occurred (15 more days on written good cause given to the Department within 30 days)
notify: Affected Florida residents by mail or email (never to a compromised mailbox)
clock_starts: Determination of the breach or reason to believe one occurred

obligation: Florida deemed compliance through a federal regulator's notice rules (worked example)
trigger: Notice given under the rules of the primary or functional federal regulator
deadline: Not usable here: the FTC Safeguards Rule has no individual notice procedure, so Florida individual notice is still required
notify: n/a

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs (worked example)
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 30 days after determination (the 15-day extension applies only to individual notice)
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs (synopsis, count, services offered, copy of the notice, contact)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if 500 or more Florida residents
clock_starts: Determination of the breach or reason to believe one occurred

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies (worked example)
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
notify: All nationwide consumer reporting agencies (timing, distribution, and content of the notices)

trigger: After investigation and consultation with law enforcement, the company reasonably determines the breach has not and will not likely result in identity theft or other financial harm
deadline: Written determination kept at least 5 years; provided to the Department within 30 days after the determination
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs
applies_at_this_tier: Only if that determination is made

trigger: A law enforcement agency determines in writing that individual notice would interfere with a criminal investigation
deadline: Delay individual notice for the period in the agency's written request
notify: Hold individual notices; keep the request

obligation: Florida third-party agent notice to the company (worked example)
trigger: Breach of a system maintained by a vendor acting as third-party agent
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 10 days after the agent's determination
notify: The company
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - vendors holding Florida residents' personal information

obligation: Florida Real Estate Commission notice of an escrow dispute (worked example)
citation: Fla. Stat. 475.25(1)(d)1.; Fla. Admin. Code r. 61J2-10.032(1)
trigger: A diverted or missing earnest money deposit leads to conflicting demands or good-faith doubt about funds in a brokerage sales escrow account
deadline: Written notice to the Commission within 15 business days of the last demand or of the good-faith doubt; start a settlement procedure within 30 business days
notify: Florida Real Estate Commission (by the Florida Broker of Record)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if the brokerage holds the deposit and demands conflict; other states apply their own rules
owner: Florida Broker of Record (with each state's broker of record)

citation: Title agency agreements and closing protection letter terms (contract)
trigger: Loss or suspected loss of trust account funds, or a buyer or lender claim
deadline: Per each agency agreement (treat as same day)
notify: Underwriters' agency and claims contacts

trigger: Suspected compromise of bank channels, credentials, or payment files
deadline: Per agreement (treat as immediate)
notify: The 5 trust banks' fraud and treasury contacts

obligation: SL-1 business client notice (lenders, other brokerages, homebuilders)
trigger: Incident affecting settlement services or client data
deadline: Per client agreement (standard term: 72 hours for a security incident affecting their transactions)
notify: About 1,900 business clients with open files

trigger: Incident affecting relocation services or relocating employees' data
deadline: Per client agreement
notify: About 280 corporate clients
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if SYS-13 or relocation data is affected

citation: Cyber insurance and commercial crime (funds transfer fraud) policies (contract)
trigger: Suspected security incident or funds transfer fraud
deadline: Per policy (call the carrier hotline before hiring vendors)
notify: Carriers' claims hotlines

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom or extortion payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Any extortion or ransom payment is considered
deadline: Before any payment
notify: OFAC (license request if a sanctioned party is involved); FBI or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: No for BEC; applies only if the incident turns into extortion

obligation: CIRCIA incident and ransom payment reports
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours (incident); 24 hours after a ransom payment
notify: CISA
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-09-25; reporting is voluntary

trigger: Non-financed transfer to an entity or trust with Title and Escrow as settlement agent
deadline: Not in effect
notify: FinCEN
applies_at_this_tier: No - rule vacated 2026-03-19; appeal pending (P03 G-062)

obligation: Covered telecommunications equipment or services discovered
citation: FAR 52.204-25(d); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Covered telecommunications equipment or services found in federal contract performance
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification, then a further report within 10 business days. Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
notify: Contracting officer
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company holds no federal contracts; recheck if contracts are signed
